contexts.text: Parched with the east wind () = full of cupidities... In the genuine sense, the east wind, and the east = love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour; hence in the opposite sense, they = the love of self and the love of the world, and therefore concupiscences and cupidities.
That the east wind, or a wind of the east = those things which are of cupidities and thence of phantasies. Illustrated.
Here, wind = phantasies; and east wind, cupidities.
To pursue the east wind () = to multiply vastation.
A state of vastation and temptation is also called the day of the east wind ().
To pursue the east wind, etc. = to falsify truths.
The wind () = falsity; and the east wind = falsity drying up and dissipating truths. AE 654:58.
The east wind from the wilderness () = its destruction from the fallacies which are from external sensuous things.
An east wind, the wind of Jehovah () = the ardour of cupidity from the love and conceit of destroying truths.
